subject: Warning in measurement invariance analysis with paired sample and ordinal indicator variables

messages.author: 1f1b0314d9e6ab9b
messages.subject: Warning in measurement invariance analysis with paired sample and ordinal indicator variables
parts:
Hello,

I am using lavaan to evaluate measurement invariance of a single factor scale with a sample composed of fathers and mothers from the same families. I have six ordinal indicator variables, and the basic, equal form model is defined as:

model1 <- "
fDisc.P =~ QOM.P.4 + QOM.P.7 + QOM.P.8 + QOM.P.11 + QOM.P.18 + QOM.P.25
fDisc.M =~ QOM.M.4 + QOM.M.7 + QOM.M.8 + QOM.M.11 + QOM.M.18 + QOM.M.25

fDisc.P ~~ fDisc.M

QOM.P.4 ~~ QOM.M.4
QOM.P.7 ~~ QOM.M.7
QOM.P.8 ~~ QOM.M.8
QOM.P.11 ~~ QOM.M.11
QOM.P.18 ~~ QOM.M.18
QOM.P.25 ~~ QOM.M.25
"
modelFitFull <- cfa(model1, data=qomPar, estimator='WLSMV',
                ordered = c(paste('QOM.P.', c(4, 7, 8, 11, 18, 25), sep=''),
                paste('QOM.M.', c(4, 7, 8, 11, 18, 25), sep='')))

Indicators and factor covariances are added in a similar way to a longitudinal model, to account for dependence between subjects from the same family.
The model fits with some warnings because of empty cells in bivariate tables, but the fit indices are reasonably good.

For the second model, as usual, I free the loadings from all indicator but constrain them to be the same for both fathers and mothers; I keep one latent variable variance fixed at 1 and the other free.

model2 <- "
fDisc.P =~ NA*QOM.P.4 + l1*QOM.P.4 + l2*QOM.P.7 + l3*QOM.P.8 + l4*QOM.P.11 + l5*QOM.P.18 + l6*QOM.P.25
fDisc.M =~ NA*QOM.M.4 + l1*QOM.M.4 + l2*QOM.M.7 + l3*QOM.M.8 + l4*QOM.M.11 + l5*QOM.M.18 + l6*QOM.M.25
  
fDisc.P ~~ fDisc.M
 
fDisc.P ~~ 1*fDisc.P 
fDisc.M ~~ NA*fDisc.M 

QOM.P.4 ~~ QOM.M.4
QOM.P.7 ~~ QOM.M.7
QOM.P.8 ~~ QOM.M.8
QOM.P.11 ~~ QOM.M.11
QOM.P.18 ~~ QOM.M.18
QOM.P.25 ~~ QOM.M.25
"
modelFitLoad <- cfa(model2, data=qomPar, estimator='WLSMV',
                    ordered = c(paste('QOM.P.', c(4, 7, 8, 11, 18, 25), sep=''),
                                paste('QOM.M.', c(4, 7, 8, 11, 18, 25), sep='')))

Again, the model fit is very good, and the warnings about zero counts are the only issue I have so far.

But, when I try to compare both models via the 'anova' function, I get the following warning:
Warning message:
In lav_partable_constraints_ceq(P0, txtOnly = TRUE) :
  lavaan WARNING: non-free parameter(s) in equality constraint(s): .p1. .p7.

Both (internal) parameter refer to the loadings of the first indicator variables, but the syntax explicitly frees them (via 'NA') and adds the constraint (via parameter label). The LR table shows both DF and Chisq for both models, but offers no information on model comparison. If I simply free both parameters but don't constrain them (as suggested in another thread), the model comparison displays as expected. Is there anything wrong with the model definition or how I am fitting them?

I tried to investigate and noticed that, when I estimate the first indicator parameter and constrain it, the 'lav_partable_constraints_ceq' function (or rather, the function that calls it, lav_test_diff_af_h1) returns this function:

function (.x., ...) 
{
    out <- numeric(0L)
    .p1. <- NA
    .p7. <- NA
    .p2. <- .x.[1]
    .p3. <- .x.[2]
    .p4. <- .x.[3]
    .p5. <- .x.[4]
    .p6. <- .x.[5]
    .p8. <- .x.[6]
    .p9. <- .x.[7]
    .p10. <- .x.[8]
    .p11. <- .x.[9]
    .p12. <- .x.[10]
    out[1] <- .p1. - (.p7.)
    out[2] <- .p2. - (.p8.)
    out[3] <- .p3. - (.p9.)
    out[4] <- .p4. - (.p10.)
    out[5] <- .p5. - (.p11.)
    out[6] <- .p6. - (.p12.)
    out[7] = .x.[78] - 1
    return(out)
}
<environment: 0x7609ce8>

But if I fit the model without the constraint, the function has no 'NA's:

function (.x., ...) 
{
    out <- numeric(0L)
    .p2. <- .x.[1]
    .p3. <- .x.[2]
    .p4. <- .x.[3]
    .p5. <- .x.[4]
    .p6. <- .x.[5]
    .p8. <- .x.[6]
    .p9. <- .x.[7]
    .p10. <- .x.[8]
    .p11. <- .x.[9]
    .p12. <- .x.[10]
    out[1] <- .p2. - (.p8.)
    out[2] <- .p3. - (.p9.)
    out[3] <- .p4. - (.p10.)
    out[4] <- .p5. - (.p11.)
    out[5] <- .p6. - (.p12.)
    out[6] = .x.[78] - 1
    return(out)
}
<environment: 0x8b8d658>

And, indeed, if I call the lavTestLRT function with parameter A.method='delta', the Chisq Diff is computed. What is happening with the plain anova?

Thanks,
Erikson
